searchText: Hi everyone, I'm currently investigating whether the possibility of implementing a prototype of verkle tries in a client would make a good <#843176491386667018> project. From what I've read so far it seems that the overall design of verkle tries is basically agreed upon and the remaining questions are details that can be worked out as we develop a prototype or that would benefit from benchmarking with a real implementation (e.g. 256 vs 1024 degree trees). Does this seem reasonable? Do you know if anyone is working on anything that might clash with this? So there is a real implementation and we're in the process of getting some "real benchmarks" at least for abstract key/value reads/writes Making a next step of plugging that into an ethereum client would definitely make sense! I'm trying to understand the proposal here: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/proposed-verkle-tree-scheme-for-ethereum-state/5805 It seems that the second line here: ``` def get_basic_data_tree_key(address, i): assert 0 <= i < 256 return address[:3] + hash(address + b'\x00')[:27] + i.to_bytes(2, 'big') ``` should really be ```assert 0 <= i < 65536``` or am I misunderstanding something? Aaah yes it should be You are right So one thing that we are thinking right now is whether to do width=8 or width=10. If we do width=10, then we don't need these depth-2 subtrees, as 32 * 1024 is big enough to fit a full header and code and a few subtrees Also, even if we do width=8, there's a chance we may want to move to a depth-1 subtree model where the code is still split across a few pieces I presume you are referring to https://github.com/ethereum/research/tree/master/verkle_trie <@!243183686562873344> there is also https://github.com/gballet/go-verkle and https://github.com/crate-crypto/rust-verkle sharing this here : https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/code-chunk-cost-analysis this is an analysis of the impact of charging 350/330 gas for accessing individual code chunks, the analysis shows the increase in block level, and also in transaction level for the most gas-consuming contracts. there is also a relevant conversation on the <#706868829900505180> channel

excerpts.content:
Hi everyone, I'm currently investigating whether the possibility of implementing a prototype of verkle tries in a client would make a good <#843176491386667018> project.

From what I've read so far it seems that the overall design of verkle tries is basically agreed upon and the remaining questions are details that can be worked out as we develop a prototype or that would benefit from benchmarking with a real implementation (e.g. 256 vs 1024 degree trees).

Does this seem reasonable? Do you know if anyone is working on anything that might clash with this?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: So there is a real implementation and we're in the process of getting some "real benchmarks" at least for abstract key/value reads/writes

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Making a next step of plugging that into an ethereum client would definitely make sense!

```

    assert 0 <= i < 256
    return address[:3] + hash(address + b'\x00')[:27] + 
i.to_bytes(2, 'big')
```

or am I misunderstanding something?
